title: Embeddings/rerank debug: dim mismatch + latency spikes (scratch)
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs while investigating two related anomalies on /rerank endpoint: 1) occasional dimension mismatch errors (index vs embedding) and 2) intermittent latency spikes (p95 up to ~180ms from baseline ~40-50ms).

Summary so far:
- Incident window: started 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC, recurring spikes and a handful of user-facing rerank errors.
- Error seen in user logs: ValueError: Expected embedding dim 1536, got 1024 (trace below). Not consistent across all requests.
- Metrics: normal p50 ~45ms, p95 jumps to ~180ms for ~10% of requests during window. CPU on rerank workers shows short bursts; GPU serving for embeddings looks steady.
- Quick hypothesis (primary): embedding model used by caller or internal upstream routing changed for some requests (1536 -> 1024). Index built with 1536 vectors (old model), so mismatch when we try to score.
- Secondary hypothesis for latency: small-batch path and synchronous Python scoring on CPU triggered by fallback path (e.g., when cached scores aren't available), or occasional GC/heap pressure on rerank pods. Also possible routing to a different container instance with older code that does CPU scoring.

Commands / repro attempts (local):
1) curl repro to hosted embeddings endpoint (explicit model param):
   curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":"test sentence"}' | jq -r '.data[0].embedding | length'
   -> returns 1536 (expected)

2) curl w/o model param (let routing happen):
   curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"test sentence"}' | jq -r '.data[0].embedding | length'
   -> returned 1024 in one run (repro intermittent).
   Notes: suggests default/model routing sometimes picks a 1024 model. Need to check default model config and rollout flags.

3) local Python script to fetch embedding shapes for a batch of test inputs and print model metadata:
   # snippet
   from redwood_client import Client
   c = Client(api_key='REDACTED')
   resp = c.embeddings.create(input=["a","b","c"], model=None)
   for i in resp.data:
       print(i.index, len(i.embedding), resp.meta.get('model'))

   -> Output (sample):
      0 1536 text-embedding-3-large
      1 1024 text-embedding-2-medium
      2 1536 text-embedding-3-large
   -> confirms mixed model assignments in same batch.

4) Check rerank service logs when error occurs (matched request-id):
   2026-03-11T03:22:15.342Z request-id=abc123 level=error msg="embedding dim mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024"
   stack: ValueError: Expected embedding dim 1536, got 1024
          at rerank.score (rerank/scorer.py:87)
          at rerank.handler (rerank/handler.py:54)

5) Check index metadata (FAISS index stored in s3):
   aws s3 cp s3://emb-indexes/re-rank-v2/metadata.json -
   -> metadata shows vector_dim = 1536, model_tag = text-embedding-3-large@2026-02-20

6) Query index health API:
   GET /internal/indexes/re-rank-v2/health -> OK, last_rebuild=2026-02-20T02:00:00Z

7) Trace through request routing (smart router logs):
   - Found rollout config change on 2026-03-10 toggling default-embeddings-model to "auto" (RINF-2129) to allow gradual migration.
   - Router sometimes chooses cheaper 1024 model for small payloads. That explains mixed dims.

Latency breadcrumbs:
- Prometheus metrics (rerank service):
  - baseline: p50=43ms p95=58ms (normal)
  - incident: p50=45ms p95=178ms (spike tail)
- Flamegraphs for one spike showed:
  - ~60% time spent in serialization + network (retry path), ~35% in score computation (Python dot-product), ~5% other.
- CPU profile: short-lived 100% CPU on one core for ~120-200ms during spikes. Heap allocation increased slightly.
- K8s event at same time: node kubelet GC logs, but not full OOM.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Pinned embeddings model for rerank service requests by adding explicit model param to rerank client (PR: re-rank/pull/432) to force 1536 model until router rollout is stable.
- Added validation in rerank handler: if embedding length != index_dim -> return 400 with actionable message and capture metrics for rate. This reduces 500s.

What worked / produced signal:
- Forcing model param removed dim mismatch errors in canary traffic.
- Rebuilding index with 1024 vectors also works, but that is heavy and will lower quality; not acceptable unless we intentionally switch models.
- Router config inspection showed "auto" allowed different model assignments based on cost heuristics. Revert/latest rollout flag appears to be the root cause for dim mismatch.

Open questions / next steps:
- Why did router start assigning 1024 in same batch? Is there a bug in batching + routing where each item in batch is routed independently rather than the batch-level model decision? (Suspect: router does per-item policy evaluation).
- Verify if batching path in embeddings service is preserving per-batch model decision or doing per-item. Need to check batching code in serving runtime (serving-runtime/batcher.go).
- Investigate latency spike root cause further: is it caused by fallback CPU scoring when embeddings are missing or when mismatch triggers extra validation? Capture full trace for a spike (request-id alpha).
- Add test in CI that validates embedding dims for end-to-end rerank + index against pinned model.

Notes/TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add temporary kill-switch to router rollout flag (rollback auto -> default=text-embedding-3-large) (action: Aran)
- [x] Patch rerank client to send model param (merged) (Maya)
- [ ] Add metric/alert: embedding_dim_mismatch_rate > 0.01% (Evelyn)
- [ ] Add unit/integration test around batch-level routing decision (Liam)
- [ ] Investigate whether small-batch path picks CPU scorer (SRE/serving-runtime)

Useful snippets saved:
- Repro script: scripts/repro/embedding-dim-check.py
- Logs filtered by request-id: grep "embedding dim mismatch" /var/log/rerank/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'

Slack and tickets:
- Slack thread: #eng-embeddings (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02ABCD1234/p164698)
- Jira: RINF-2147 (tracking dim mismatch incident), RINF-2150 (followup latency investigation)

Hypotheses prioritized: 
1) Router rollout -> mixed model assignment -> dim mismatch errors (HIGH confidence, supported by local repro and rollout log).
2) Latency spikes mostly orthogonal but sometimes correlated when rerank triggers extra validation/fallback -> some spikes resolved by pinning model (MED confidence).
3) Secondary latency contributor: occasional pod-level CPU spike (GC or single-core tight loop) -> needs profiling (LOW-MED).

If I return to this later: capture full trace for both error and spike with request-id mapping (trace ID + span), collect heap/CPU profile of rerank pod at spike time, and check batcher code in embeddings service to ensure consistent per-batch model decisions.

Notes-to-self: keep scratch notes in Drive; final postmortem should include timeline, blast radius (what customers saw), mitigation, root cause, and long-term fixes (router guardrails + CI tests + alerts).

-- Maya
